newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian investors launch new pan-Arab daily.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian investors launch new pan-Arab daily.

text.p: A new Jordanian daily paper, Al Arab al-Yawm, hit the newstands on Saturday and has ambitious plans to join a growing number of Middle Eastern papers with local editions across the region, its publishers said.

Riyad al-Hroub, the newspaper's editor-in-chief and a shareholder, told reporters the paper hoped to be a pan-Arab paper which would be printed in regional capitals such as Dubai and Cairo and Western capitals with large Arab communities.

The paper joins four daily papers, Al-Rai, Ad-Dustour, al-Aswaq and the English language Jordan Times, and many independent weekly newspapers set up since Jordan lifted martial law in 1989, in a country of just four million people.

The new daily wants to compete with Arab media groups such as the London-based Saudi-owned daily Al Hayat and Sharq al-Awsat, which have locally printed editions in the main Arab capitals and Western cities where large Arab communities live.

Hroub said Al Arab al-Yawm (The Arab Today) is the first newspaper to be launched by Al Dar al-Watniyah Press, a public shareholding company which has ambitious plans to become a media conglomerate embracing television and radio.
The company plans to triple its initial four million dinar ($5.6 million) capital to 12 million dinars ($16.9 million) as it expands its media business, Hroub said.

Al Arab al-Yawm also plans to set up a sister publication in Palestinian self-rule areas after Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat gave his blessing to its publication from offices in Arab East Jerusalem, Hroub said.
